items.title: Michael Moore interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: I mean I grew up with the Nat Cole Trio. My father had a trio based like that

ctx.x: I feel the same way. Like T.S. Monk’s band, you know Thelonious Monk Junior, I mean I heard them and they have arrangements and they’re not reading music, they have their

act together. And the improvisation is very good, but there are a lot of great improvisers around nowadays, but there are very few bands. And my looking back in history, I mean I grew up with the Nat Cole Trio. My father had a trio based like that, on that kind of thing, and those tight arrangements. And Benny Goodman’s trios and quartets and all the groups that I admired as I grew up were very well thought out and very well rehearsed, and the improvisation was a great part of it but so were the arrangements.…
You went with Woody Herman at a pretty early age.
